newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MPs need more data on British missile deal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MPs need more data on British missile deal.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament is demanding the government provide it with more details of a planned missile deal with British Aerospace Plc, an MP said on Sunday.
Nasser al-Sanea, head of parliament's finance committee, told Reuters the controversial issue should be further probed by MPs before the government finalises the deal.
The government exercised its executive right earlier this month and ..."put in motion a process to finalise the deal which is difficult to stop," said a Western industry expert.
However, the Kuwait daily al-Qabas reported on Sunday that the government had put the deal for Sea Skua missiles for the Kuwait Navy on hold after pressure from MPs.
Sanea said:"Information given to us so far is insufficient. If the government convinces us that everything about the deal was done in a correct way then there will be no objections."
Industry experts said parts of the deal were initialled but the final format is yet to be signed.

Parliament, following moves by the previous assembly, is locked with the government in a war of wills over the deal. The government last month told the house the decision to buy the Sea Skuas was final, droping a cheaper offer for France's Aerospatiale MM-15 missile.

Kuwait newspapers have said the deal was for around $90 million but experts said the contract was split into several parts, including training and a British gift of 20 Sea Skua missiles, making it difficult to give an exact figure.
"We are not objecting to the deal with no reason. The law must be respected and procedures for concluding such deals must be followed," Sanea said by telephone.
He said as of last Wednesday the government had not asked for the required approval by the state's Audit Bureau, a watchdog body which reports to parliament.
Although MPs have limited ability to scrap the deal they can increase pressure on the government, political sources say.

"I do not think parliament will be quiet...Politically there are things we can do. We must discuss the deal with the defence minister (Sheikh Salem Sabah al-Salem al-Sabah), even in the corridors (of parliament)," Sanea said.
Parliament was due to discuss the deal earlier this month but postponed the debate until Sheikh Salem returns from a private visit to London.
The missiles will arm Kuwait's eight, French-made $500 million fast patrol boats ordered in 1995. The first of the 42- metre vessels was completed last month.
